label: L10 · What the Lecturer Flagged
rows: No percentages, case counts or mortality figures (“I'm not going to be testing you on the percentages”). No antibiotic choice (“that's what we have our PDRs [Physicians' Desk References] for”).
“What is the most common, what's the deadliest, how the different things work.”
Bacillus = CENTRAL spore. Clostridium = TERMINAL spore (drumstick, “tennis racket”).

Clostridium perfringens = commonest gas gangrene; mixed infection; floppy baby syndrome; diphtheria pseudomembrane; Propionibacterium → Cutibacterium; three stages of tuberculosis; Actinomyces israelii harmful only in deeper tissue.
Names of the 17 myonecrosis toxins (know what they do) · Erysipelothrix (slides 57–58) · Mycobacterium species chart (slide 68) · non-tuberculous mycobacteria (slide 90).

label: L10 · Sorting the Gram-Positive Bacilli
rows: Endospores and acid-fastness → spore-formers, regular non-spore-formers, irregular non-spore-formers.
Aerobic (or facultative), catalase POSITIVE, central spore, soil saprobe; makes bacitracin, gramicidin, subtilin.
Obligately anaerobic, catalase NEGATIVE, terminal spore made only under anaerobic conditions; among the most toxic exotoxins on earth.
Stain uniformly, one shape: Lactobacillus, Listeria, Erysipelothrix.
Pleomorphic, stain unevenly: Corynebacterium, Cutibacterium, Mycobacterium (acid-fast), Actinomyces and Nocardia (filamentous). Corynebacterium and Mycobacterium have mycolic acids.

label: L10 · Bacillus anthracis & Bacillus cereus
rows: Large block-shaped rods in chains, central spores; Koch's postulates; zoonosis; Category A bioterrorism agent; polypeptide capsule.
Protective antigen = receptor site for the other two · edema factor impairs phagocytosis · lethal factor lyses macrophages at high levels → cytokine surge → septic-shock picture.
MOST COMMON. Spores through a cut → painless papule → ulcer with vesicles → black necrotic eschar.
DEADLIEST. Woolsorters' disease: inhaled spores; macrophages die en masse; shock; half get meningitis.
Gastrointestinal = eaten infected meat (mouth and esophageal ulcers). Injection = heroin, deep muscle. Meningitis can follow ANY form.
Pulmonary also gets antitoxin. Biothrax = purified toxoid for high-risk workers and military (not under 18 or over 65); livestock get live spores.
Foodborne (rice, potatoes, meat); spores survive cooking and reheating. Diarrheal = large protein toxin; emetic = small heat-stable peptide. About 24 hours, no treatment.
Sepsis from contaminated alcohol prep pads · eye infections, pneumonia · welder's anthrax = anthrax toxin made by B. cereus.

label: L10 · Gas Gangrene, Tetanus & Botulism
rows: Clostridium perfringens. Needs dead tissue + low oxygen: deep dirty wounds, compound fractures. ★ MIXED infection — aerobes use up the oxygen.
Gas = fermented muscle carbohydrate. Spread = collagenase, hyaluronidase. Cellulitis stays local; true myonecrosis spreads with fever and necrosis. Debride, hyperbaric oxygen; NO vaccine.
Meat, fish; toxin made IN THE INTESTINE; mild, rapid recovery. Botulism = rare but severe.

Puncture wounds, umbilical stump (neonates). Tetanospasmin blocks gamma-aminobutyric acid and glycine → UNCONTROLLED contraction; death by respiratory failure (spasm of the breathing muscles and larynx). Shorter incubation = worse.
Antitoxin neutralizes CIRCULATING, not bound, toxin; muscle relaxants; booster every 10 years. Commonest in older adults and drug users.
Botulin blocks ACETYLCHOLINE at the junction → DESCENDING flaccid paralysis. Double vision, trouble swallowing first. Ventilators cut mortality.
Low-acid home-canned food (air out, spores survive). ★ Infant = MOST COMMON: swallowed spores, honey → floppy baby. Wound = black tar heroin. Iatrogenic = medical toxin use.
Antitoxin + cardiac and respiratory support. Prevent: discard bulging cans, boil home-bottled food 10 minutes.

label: L10 · C. difficile, Lactobacillus & Listeria
rows: Clostridioides (split off by ribonucleic acid sequencing). Low-number colon resident; broad-spectrum antibiotics kill competitors → overgrowth → enterotoxins.
Pseudomembranous colitis (sloughed necrotic lining), toxic megacolon, perforation. Major hospital diarrhea. Risk: antibiotics, long stays, age, gastric acid inhibitors.
Mild: fluids + stop the antibiotic. Fecal microbiota transplant restores flora. Precautions against spread.
Gut and vaginal flora; lactic acid, acetic acid, hydrogen peroxide. Antibiotics → opportunist superinfection.
Coccobacilli to filaments, no capsule. GROWS IN THE FRIDGE. Replicates in host cytoplasm → avoids antibody. Soil, water, animal gut → dairy, poultry, meat.
Mild in healthy adults; brain and meninges in the immunocompromised, fetuses, neonates. Culture = cold enrichment. Prevent = pasteurize and cook.

label: L10 · Diphtheria & Cutibacterium
rows: Healthy carriers; respiratory droplets; non-immunized children in crowding.
Solidified inflammatory fluid in the throat — characteristic; can asphyxiate.
Targets the HEART (myocarditis) and NERVES (weakness, paralysis).
Palisades, granules; alkaline methylene blue. Horse-serum antitoxin neutralizes circulating toxin only. Prevent: toxoid series + boosters.
Formerly Propionibacterium. Pilosebaceous glands; nontoxigenic; acne via inflammatory mediators.
Biofilm on prosthetics; grows over 6 days, needs prolonged anaerobic culture; hardware removal, debridement, months of antibiotics.

label: L10 · Tuberculosis & Leprosy
rows: Acid-fast (mycolic acids, waxes); strict aerobes; catalase; no capsules, flagella or spores; slow.
No exotoxins; waxes + cord factor resist macrophages. Airborne droplets; infectious dose about 10 cells. Latent = not contagious, can reactivate.
PRIMARY: tubercles (granulomas), caseous lesions calcify. SECONDARY: reactivation, tubercles drain into bronchi, “consumption”. DISSEMINATED: nodes, kidneys, bones, meninges.
Mantoux read at 48–72 hours (type IV). QuantiFERON = gamma interferon. False +: BCG (bacille Calmette-Guérin), other mycobacteria. False −: too early, immunosuppression. Ziehl-Neelsen sputum.
Two or more drugs for months; vaccine = attenuated Mycobacterium bovis (used abroad).
Not cultivable → armadillos; slowest growing; globi; skin macrophages and Schwann cells. Transmission not fully verified; armadillos possible.
TUBERCULOID (T helper 1): shallow lesions, local pain loss. LEPROMATOUS (T helper 2): nodular, disseminated, T cells barely respond; treated far longer.
Numbness, lost heat and cold sense, thick earlobes, stuffy nose; acid-fast bacilli in lesions; feather test.

label: L10 · Actinomyces, Nocardia & Transmission
rows: Actinomyces and Nocardia: nonmotile, filamentous, related to mycobacteria.
Harmless mouth, gut, genital resident — disease only in DEEPER tissue. Cervicofacial ← oral infection · thoracic · abdominal ← burst appendix · uterine ← intrauterine device.
Pulmonary disease like tuberculosis (can cross the chest wall to brain, kidneys); mycetoma = deep granulomatous inflammation.

Cut, inhaled, eaten, injected spores (anthrax) · food (B. cereus, Listeria, botulism) · deep wounds (perfringens, tetanus) · own flora after antibiotics (C. difficile) · droplets (diphtheria, tuberculosis) · armadillos? (leprosy) · deeper tissue (Actinomyces).
